revisions.title: Hippothales’s songs fill the company’s ears
revisions.body: Ctesippus’s image concerns the ears of the companions gathered with him, not everyone without qualification.

revisions.title: Desire and Harm
revisions.body: The passage does not present desire as harmless: a desire can be harmful. Desire alone therefore cannot establish that its object is good.

body: "Harmless desire survives even if bad disappears, so bad cannot be friendship's cause. Socrates offers desire as a new candidate, then connects it to need: what lacks something desires it, and the lacking thing is drawn toward its own (oikeion). For Lysis and Menexenus, this makes them akin in some way, but the relation remains open—perhaps soul, character, manner, or form—and is not yet a final definition."
